info.title: BestAppify API
info.description:
Shopify App Store intelligence for app developers: keyword rankings, competitors,
review analysis, listing analytics and revenue — for your own apps and for the market.

Authenticate with an API key from https://bestappify.app/dashboard/api as
`Authorization: Bearer ba_live_…`.

Rate limits: 120 requests per minute; daily allowance by plan — 100 on Free, 1,000 on Growth, 10,000 on Pro. Counted per account across all keys.

Error codes: missing_api_key (401), invalid_api_key (401), rate_limited (429), daily_limit_reached (429), app_not_found (404), keyword_not_tracked (404), keyword_not_found (404), category_not_found (404), missing_query (400), app_not_in_catalog (409), service_unavailable (503), internal_error (500), upgrade_required (402), review_limit_reached (429), nothing_to_review (400), invalid_body (400).

get.summary: Your account, apps and rate limits
get.description: Confirms the key works and returns the app references every other endpoint accepts, plus how much of your rate limit you have used.
Every programme on your account with its payout terms and 30 days of analytics — link views, conversions, revenue and commission per affiliate. Empty when you run none.
Every referred install and sale credited on a programme, each row carrying the commission rate frozen at the moment it was recorded — so a figure can be audited rather than trusted.

get.summary: What you have earned promoting apps
get.description: Your side of the marketplace: totals and daily series, the individual referrals behind them, and your payout balance per programme. Scoped to your own account.
Every app on your account. The `app` field is the handle used in the paths below; `tracked_app_id` and `app_id` are returned for callers that prefer ids.

Your tracked keywords for one app with today's position, the week-over-week change, and the difficulty, competition and demand indices. `position` is the live standing and is null when the app did not appear in the latest crawl. `last_known_position` and `change` come from the rank history keyed to your app in our catalog; `is_current: false` means that history is a little behind the newest crawl, not that the app stopped ranking.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to csv for a CSV download.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: App handle, listing URL, tracked_app_id or app_id.

get.summary: One keyword, with full rank history
get.description: Daily rank history for a single tracked keyword, oldest first, plus its current standing. `{keyword}` is the term (URL-encoded) or its keyword_id.

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: Keyword term, URL-encoded, or its keyword_id.

get.description: Keywords one of your tracked competitors ranks for and this app does not, with the competitor's position.
Your tracked competitor set with current rank and rank change, plus the keyword overlap matrix showing where each of you places.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to csv for a CSV download.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Set to `timeline` to also return the daily rank timeline for every app.

get.description: Rating distribution, monthly review trend, countries, the AI theme analysis (what merchants love, complain about and ask for) and a comparison against your tracked competitors.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to csv for a CSV download.

parameters.name: recent
parameters.description: How many individual recent reviews to include. Default 10, max 50.

get.description: Listing views, install clicks, installs, click-through and conversion from the Google Analytics property linked to the app, daily and totalled. Returns `connected: false` when no property is linked.

get.summary: Real merchant searches and the positions they saw
get.description: The search terms merchants actually typed to reach your listing, the position they actually saw (with Shopify's sponsored slots removed so it matches organic rank), plus device, country, locale and Install clicks per term. Read from the Google Analytics property linked to the app. This is the merchant's own answer, not our crawler's — `/keywords` is the crawler, works for any app including competitors, and needs no setup. Add `?format=csv` for a spreadsheet. Returns `connected: false` when no property is linked.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Filter to one device: desktop, mobile or tablet.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Filter to one ISO country code.

parameters.name: search_type
parameters.description: Filter to organic, paid, ai or other.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to `csv` for a CSV download.

get.summary: Keyword headroom, weighted by how beatable the field is
get.description: Ranks the terms already sending you traffic by how much more they could send. Estimates the demand behind your current views, asks what position 3 would have yielded, then discounts it by how strong the apps ranked above you are according to our own weekly crawl — `winnability`, `apps_above` and `median_reviews_above` are that discount, and no GA4-only tool can compute them. Scores are relative within one app's keywords, never across apps. Add `?format=csv` for a spreadsheet.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to `csv` for a CSV download.

get.summary: Week-over-week search traffic, including what stopped
get.description: The same comparison as the Tuesday email, as data: views and Install clicks this week against last, per traffic source and per keyword, with `gained`, `lost`, `new` and — the one most worth automating against — `stopped`, the terms that drove traffic last week and none this week. The window is fixed at two seven-day periods ending three days ago because Google keeps revising recent days; `window` gives the exact dates.

get.summary: Which store installed, and how it found you
get.description: Installs resolved to the store that made them: shop domain, shop id, date, device, country, and the search term most likely behind it (labelled as the inference it is — Shopify's install event is server-side and carries no page). Pass `shop_url` up to 50 times, or once comma-separated, to check specific stores; `not_found` lists the ones we have no install for. Needs `shop_url` registered as a GA4 custom dimension — when it isn't, the response says so in `note` rather than returning an empty list that looks like zero installs.

parameters.name: shop_url
parameters.description: Shop domain to look up. Repeatable, or comma-separated. Up to 50. Omit for every store.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to `csv` for a CSV download.

get.description: Monthly MRR, churn rate, trials, installs, uninstalls and net revenue from the Shopify Partner API. MRR and churn are derived from the subscription charge lifecycle — the Partner API publishes neither directly. Returns `connected: false` when the app is not linked to a Partner app.
Rank trajectory over time, position in each category, nearest competitors by category rank, and how the app's entry price compares with its peers.

get.summary: Shopify Community threads that mention your apps
get.description: Forum posts matching your apps' names or the keywords you track — most usefully, merchants asking for an app like yours. `is_strong` marks the ones we would email you about (your app named, or the term in a thread title or opening post) as opposed to a term appearing in a mid-thread reply; both are returned so you can apply your own bar. Add ?format=csv for a spreadsheet.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: active (default, hides dismissed), unread, dismissed, or all.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to csv for a CSV download.

get.summary: What changed on your listings — and your competitors'
get.description: Dated App Store listing changes for your apps and the rivals you track: taglines, descriptions, icons, screenshots, integrations, and listings leaving the store. `is_mine` separates yours from theirs. Covers competitors because it reads our own catalog crawl rather than your analytics — so these are events you can line up against your rank history. Only includes changes since we began recording. Add ?format=csv for a spreadsheet.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to csv for a CSV download.

get.description: Search every app we hold by name — not only your own. This is how you find a competitor's handle before looking it up.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term matched against the app name.

get.description: Any app in our catalog by handle, listing URL or id: rating, review count, description, categories, pricing plans and listing status.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: App handle, listing URL or id.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Set to `intelligence` to add rank trajectory and the pricing benchmark.

get.description: The App Store leaderboard, overall or for one category. Ranked by review count, because Shopify publishes no install numbers.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to csv for a CSV download.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category id or exact title. Omit for the overall board.

get.description: Which apps climbed and which fell over the last week, from our daily rank snapshots. `change` is positive for a climb; `rank_a_week_ago: null` marks an app new to the ranking.

Every keyword merchants search on the App Store, harvested from the store's own autocomplete, with how many apps rank for it, who leads, and the difficulty, competition and demand indices. `demand` and `difficulty` are relative 0-100 indices built from the review volume of each term's top 10 — not search volume, which Shopify publishes nowhere. Add `format=csv` for a spreadsheet.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Filter to keywords containing this text.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: Brand keywords — searches for a named app — are excluded by default. `only` returns just those, `include` returns both.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Keywords to return. Default 50, max 200 (1,000 for CSV).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip, for paging. `meta.total` is the full count.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to `csv` to download instead of returning JSON.

get.description: Every app ranking for one App Store search, in order, with its rating, review count, entry price, category and the position it held a week earlier. Works for any keyword in the directory, not only ones you track.

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: The keyword, URL-encoded, or its slug. Both `product bundles` and `product-bundles` resolve.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to `csv` to download the ranked apps instead of returning JSON.

get.description: Every category with its app count, growth and the leader's share of reviews — for judging whether a niche is crowded or open.
The App Store categories we hold at least five apps for, with counts. These ids and titles are what `?category=` accepts.

get.summary: What listing edits actually do to rank
get.description: Across every app we crawl, what each kind of listing edit measurably did to search rank: how many edits of that kind were measured, the median places moved, and how the outcomes split between better, worse and no change. Correlational with small samples — read `coverage` and each field's `changes_measured` before quoting a figure, and carry the `caveat` into whatever you write.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category id or exact title to restrict to. Omit for the whole App Store.

get.summary: Who moved on this term, and what they had just changed
get.description: Every app we saw move at least N places on one search term in the window, with the listing edits we logged for it shortly before the move. An empty `listing_changes_before` means we logged no edit, not that nothing happened.

parameters.name: min_places
parameters.description: Smallest move worth reporting. Default 3, range 1-40.

get.summary: One app's edits and what each one did
get.description: Any catalog app's logged listing edits, each with the rank effect measured on the keywords it ranked for either side of the edit. Works for apps you do not own, which is how you read a competitor's playbook. `keywords_entered`/`keywords_exited` are null when `crawl_coverage_comparable` is false — our crawl volume differed too much either side for those counts to mean anything.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: Any catalog app's handle or id.

post.summary: Senior review of a listing change you are about to make
post.description: Send the change you intend to ship — new name, tagline or description, the terms it targets, and your reasoning — and get back deterministic checks plus a prioritised critique. `checks` is computed from the database and is authoritative; `review` is judgement over the same evidence. Paid plans only, capped per account per day; an identical body is served from cache and does not count against the cap.

proposed_name.description: The new app name. Shopify's limit is 30 characters.

proposed_tagline.description: The new tagline. Shopify's limit is 62 characters.

proposed_description.description: The new description, or its opening.

target_keywords.description: The terms this change is meant to win. Up to 6 are checked in depth.

plan.description: Other actions you intend to take, one per item.

rationale.description: Your own reasoning. The review attacks the reasoning too, which is where most of the value is.

get.summary: What rivals write ON their screenshots
get.description: The marketing copy painted on the listing screenshots — yours, the apps ranked above you on your category boards, and the most-reviewed apps in the App Store — transcribed off the images by a vision model, with the layout each uses. The alt-text caption is in the listing HTML anyone can fetch; the headline is not, and it is the one a merchant scrolling the gallery actually reads. Free on every plan: it returns transcriptions that already exist and never calls a model.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `category` for the apps above you, `store` for the biggest apps in the App Store, `all` for both (default).

parameters.name: max_slots
parameters.description: Screenshots per rival, from slot 1 forward. Default 6, max 20.

post.summary: Rewrite your screenshot headlines to the leaders' pattern
post.description: Names the headline formula the leading apps share — counted from their transcribed headlines, every example quoted verbatim — says whether your gallery follows it, and rewrites the slots that don't in your own voice. Paid plans only and capped per day on the same budget as the listing reviewer; an uncached run transcribes unread rival galleries and writes a review, so expect up to ninety seconds. If your client times out waiting, retry — the review is written before the response is sent, so the retry is a cache hit. Without `refresh` a cached review is served in under a second and does not count against the cap.

brand_notes.description: The voice to keep — tone, words that must appear, words to avoid. Overrides the voice inferred from your listing.

refresh.description: Send `true` to recompute instead of serving the cached review, and to transcribe the next batch of unread rival galleries.

get.summary: What we told you before, and whether it worked
get.description: Every review and proposal we have given for this app, each matched to the listing changes that landed afterwards, whether the live copy matches ours or your draft or neither, which flagged checks the live copy still fails, and the rank effect measured either side. Free on every plan — reading your own history spends no completion. Call it before starting a listing cycle; the review endpoint reads it too and will flag a repeat of advice that was ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Reviews to return, newest first. Default 10, max 30.

post.summary: Have us write the listing rewrite
post.description: Picks the terms worth going after from this app's rank data and its gaps against competitors, writes a name, tagline and description opening around them, states what the measured history suggests, and names the risks. The output is run back through the reviewer's own checks, so a failing check is authoritative over the copy. Paid plans only, same daily cap as the review endpoint.

focus_keywords.description: Terms to go after. Omit to let the data choose them.

tone.description: How the copy should read, e.g. 'plain and technical'.

notes.description: Anything the copy must or must not say.

bearerAuth.description: An API key created in the BestAppify dashboard.

tags.name: Listing reviewer
tags.description: Judgement rather than data: what listing edits measurably do to rank, and a senior review of a change before you ship it.
